refutedOnReview: REFUTED — not on the model grouping, which holds up well, but on the thing the dialect claims to be. There is no register map in either cited document, so there is no map for these eight SKUs to share.  ## What survived verification  - The Operating Manual exists at the committed path /Users/lemarier/dev/solar/docs/rolls-s48-100lfp-stack-lv-manual-rev2.0.pdf. Its changelog page confirms `2.0 \| Storage Instructions \
gotchas: NO REGISTER MAP FROM ROLLS, same as the ESS. The manual names protocols; it defines none.

This is a SEPARATE DIALECT FROM rolls-lfp-ess-48v and the evidence is hard, not inferred. Three documented differences in the same vendor's own manuals: CAN sits on RJ45 pins 7/8 here versus pins 4/5 on the ESS; the external RS-485 runs at 9600 here versus 19200 on the ESS; and RS-485 A/B sit on pins 2/1 here versus pi

The protocol menu is also different. STACK-LV Appendix A lists the selection by name in Rolls LFP Desktop V2: full support — Deye/Goodwe/Pylontech/Sol-Ark/TBB → PYLONTECH (CAN 500K), SMA → SMA (CAN 500K), Solis → SOLIS (CAN 500K), Victron Energy → VICTRON ENERGY, marked (DEFAULT) (CAN 500K), Deye/Pylontech → PYLONTECH

The default protocol is VICTRON ENERGY out of the box. For a Cabin Hub listener that means the bus is speaking Victron's CAN-bus BMS protocol unless somebody changed it — and Victron does not publish that protocol openly either.
Bluetooth exists on this model and the Rolls LFP Connect app can SET the inverter protocol on an ESS device. The BLE protocol itself is undocumented and no community implementation of it was found.
unmappedReports: charge-voltage-limit / charge-current-limit / discharge-current-limit — the closed-loop payload, and the whole point of connecting; no MetricKind can hold any of them, BMS alarm / protection / fault flags, per-cell voltages and cell delta, remaining and full-charge capacity in Ah, internal heater state, selected inverter protocol (settable from the app, readable nowhere in the contract)
